_comment: Tool calls put to `gnomon guard` AND to gnomon's own turn loop, under the same surface,
and the decision each must reach. One file, read by both sides:
packages/gnomon-core/src/guard.test.ts runs every case through runAgenticTurn (a scripted
model makes the call; an approval request means `ask`, a refusal code 2-4 means `deny`,
anything else `allow`) and through guardToolCall, and asserts the two agree with each other
and with `expect`. packages/gnomon-cli/src/guard.test.ts puts the same cases to the real
`gnomon guard` binary. A rule that moved in one place and not the other fails here.
`expect` is keyed by the [approval] gate the surface declares. A gate missing from a case
is not run under it (an allowed call under `never` really runs in the loop, and some are
not worth running: a fetch to a name that will not resolve).
The surface: `surface` below, written into a fresh git repository and committed, with
src/a.ts holding `old\n`.

surface.roles.toml:
[roles.implement]
model = "m"
tools = ["read", "write", "edit", "bash", "webfetch", "grep", "glob"]
write_allow = ["src/**", "tests/**"]
bash_deny = ['\bgit\s+push\b[^|;&]*\s(--force|-f)\b', '\brm\s+-rf\s+/']

[roles.readonly]
model = "m"
tools = ["read", "bash"]
bash_allow = ['^ls\b', '^cat\b', '^git\s+(status|diff|log)\b']

_comment: Governance levels (CONTRACTS.md §36): the same calls at each of observe, advise, prevent and
enforce, put to BOTH gnomon's own loop and `gnomon guard` (packages/gnomon-core/src/guard.test.ts,
and the real binary in packages/gnomon-cli/src/guard.test.ts). The surface is `surface` above with
policy.toml replaced by `policy` below, `{{level}}` set to the level under test.
`verdict` is what the rules say and `rule` / `family` name the first rule that says it (for an ask:
the rule that asks). `expect` is the decision per level, derived by one rule: below prevent a deny
or ask in a levelled family is allow (recorded, not applied); `rules` has a floor of prevent;
structural rules (`family` null) are never levelled. enforce decides as prevent in this build.
`decided_by` names the rule the decision reports at a level where it is not `rule`: a verdict
levelled away lets the next rule on the same call decide.
Every case is safe to RUN, because observe and advise run it: no command here reaches the
network or writes outside the scratch repository, and no case names a file that exists outside
it (`~/.aws/gnomon-conformance-absent` and `/nonexistent-…` are absent; printenv names an unset
variable). `secret_path` and `ci_path` (CONTRACTS.md §37) exist here because `[governance]` is
declared, with the default lists; grep and glob are levelled like read (family `secrets`).
`outside_root` (CONTRACTS.md §38) exists here for the same reason: its cases name a directory that
does not exist, so at observe and advise the write fails and the removal removes nothing.
levels.policy:
[approval]
gate = "on_write"
repo_code = true

[sandbox]
level = "confined"
network = false

[governance]
level = "{{level}}"
